docs.title: PGC Wiki
docs.text:
Shared reference material for the Physics graduate community at UC San Diego. This is a reference repository, not a news feed — pages here are meant to stay useful for years, and to be corrected when they drift.

Anyone can fix a page

See something wrong or out of date? Click the pencil icon at the top right of any page. It opens GitHub's web editor — no software to install. See MAINTAINING.md for the full workflow.

docs.title: Sections
docs.text: Section What lives there Onboarding Getting started as a new grad student — enrollment, TAing, first-year milestones. Resources Funding, health and wellness, campus services, and other things worth knowing exist. About What PGC is, who runs it, and how to reach us.

docs.title: What belongs here
docs.text:
Reference information that more than one person needs and that nobody wants to re-derive every year: deadlines, procedures, "who do I email about X", the unwritten norms of the department.

What does not belong here: member contact lists, financial records, or anything else you would not want publicly readable. This repository is public — see About for why.

docs.title: Privacy
docs.text:
This repository is public, and has to be — GitHub's free plan only serves Pages from public repos. Everything committed here is world-readable and stays in the git history forever, even after deletion.

Never commit

  • Member contact lists or rosters
  • Financial records, budgets tied to named people
  • Anything shared with you in confidence
  • Credentials of any kind

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Corrections are welcome from anyone. Click the pencil icon at the top right of any page to edit it in the browser, or open a pull request if you prefer. A maintainer reviews and merges; the site rebuilds automatically.

Verify before you rely on it

Deadlines and requirements change. This page is maintained by volunteers a couple of times a year. The department's official listing is authoritative; this page exists to tell you what to go look up.

docs.title: Before you arrive
docs.text:
• Accept the offer and complete the Graduate Division paperwork.
  • Set up your UCSD email and Active Directory account.
  • Complete required TA training if you are appointed as a TA.
  • Arrange housing — apply early, the queue is long.

docs.title: TAing
docs.text:
Most first-years TA. Practical notes:

  • Section prep takes longer than you expect the first time.
  • Grading load varies enormously by course — ask around before ranking preferences.
  • Know who your instructor of record is and what they expect in week one.
Collapsed detail: appointment percentages

A 50% appointment is nominally 20 hours per week averaged over the quarter. Replace this block with the real numbers and the union contract link.
